findings.description: The real prose-driven host has no executable apply-outcome failure writer. `runner.py apply-outcome` exception paths only return 1/2 without mutating loop-state; the protocol then says every non-zero mutation suppresses projection and merely tells the host to transition to ESCALATE. The recovered `apply_outcome_or_escalate()` logic is only a Python helper that reruns apply-outcome and is not exposed by `runner.py`, so the shell-driven path cannot reliably persist the failure generation — several phases such as PLAN_REVIEW and VAL_REVIEW do not even have a generic `failed` transition outcome. Thus the production host can retain the old phase and old queue generation despite the round-4 recovery claim.
findings.resolution: Expose one canonical runner command that performs apply-outcome and, on failure, atomically records the failure history, resumable ESCALATE metadata, and one sequence increment; make the host invoke it and submit-project its successful persisted-failure result. Add a runner-level test using an actual failing apply-outcome path rather than calling the Python helper directly.

findings.description: The OpenAPI projection-label schema still accepts requests the runtime deterministically rejects. Both endpoints declare any two strings of at most 160 characters, and `/work/submit` permits those labels without a projection key and with any task_type; `_projection_labels_are_valid` instead requires a projection key, `task_type == "issue"`, the first item to equal `change:<projection_key.change_id>`, the second item to equal `projection:autopilot-phase`, and that exact order. A generated client can therefore send a schema-valid request and receive 422 `invalid_projection_labels`, so the claimed runtime/OpenAPI request-constraint parity is incomplete.
findings.resolution: Encode the representable constraints with OpenAPI 3.1 JSON Schema (`prefixItems`, `const`/`pattern`, `items: false`, and conditional requirements tying labels to a projection key and issue task type), and document the cross-field equality check that JSON Schema cannot express directly. Add contract tests that validate accepted and rejected bodies against both schemas.

findings.description: Migration 038 (applied before 039) can stamp Autopilot projection labels onto a pre-existing non-`issue` row that already owns the projection key. `submit_task`/`reconcile_work_projection` validate incoming `p_task_type='issue'` when labels are present, but on `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` they select the existing key row and `UPDATE ... SET labels=p_projection_labels` with no `task_type='issue'` guard. Live suite still creates non-issue keyed rows. Claim exclusion is `task_type <> 'issue'` and `list_issues` filters `task_type=eq.issue`, so the labelled row stays claimable and board-invisible while submit/reconcile report success. Migration 039 fixes this by checking `v_existing_task_type <> 'issue'` and returning `projection_key_collision` error.
findings.resolution: Ensure migration 039 is applied after 038 in all environments. The fix in 039 adds the non-issue collision check in both submit and reconcile paths.

findings.description: A first projection generation inserted after an SSE client connects emits no refresh event in migration 038. Migration 038 inserts the canonical row with both owned labels already present, but migration 037 installs `trg_work_queue_notify` as `AFTER UPDATE` only and `notify_work_queue_change` emits `projection.labels_changed` only when OLD and NEW labels differ. With no stale row and no conflict, the initial submit performs no UPDATE, so `event_stream.py` never builds a fresh snapshot and the connected board remains stale until unrelated traffic or polling. Migration 039 adds `notify_projection_insert` trigger on `AFTER INSERT` to fix this.
findings.resolution: Ensure migration 039 is applied. The fix adds an INSERT trigger that emits `projection.labels_changed` for rows with `projection:autopilot-phase` label.

findings.description: Migration 038's `submit_task` is not an exact set-idempotent label repair despite D9 stating that both submit and reconcile clear owned labels from every noncanonical row inside the per-change transaction. On a same-generation replay, it selects and relabels only the canonical row, then returns success; it never clears `projection:autopilot-phase` from another row for the same change. Any pre-existing or externally introduced double-labelled stale row therefore survives ordinary submit replay and remains board-visible alongside the canonical row, while the adapter reports `status=ok`. Only the reconcile function contains the noncanonical cleanup. Migration 039 fixes this by adding the stale label clearing in submit_task when `p_projection_labels IS NOT NULL`.
findings.resolution: Ensure migration 039 is applied. The fix adds `UPDATE work_queue SET labels=ARRAY[]::TEXT[] WHERE id<>v_id ...` in submit_task.

findings.description: Prose-host auto `escalate_resume` authorization: SKILL.md states exit 3 means the resume was authorized and the run continues from `previous_phase`, but `runner.py` `_evaluate_gate` on `decision.proceed` only records/flushes and returns `EXIT_NO_PENDING_GATE` without `_apply_transition(..., "resolved")` or `enter_escalate` inverse. However, the current code DOES call `autopilot._apply_transition(state, "resolved", ...)` for `Gate.ESCALATE_RESUME` before saving state. The SKILL.md documentation may be outdated relative to the implementation.
findings.resolution: Verify SKILL.md matches implementation. The code correctly applies the resolved transition for ESCALATE_RESUME gate.

findings.description: Event stream backpressure handles `projection_snapshot` by immediately converting to snapshot via `_build_snapshot`, then checking window_count. If backpressure triggers in same iteration, `_build_snapshot` runs a second time (draining queue). The first snapshot result is discarded. Not a correctness issue (second snapshot is fresher) but wastes one DB-backed snapshot query during 100-row label repair bursts.
findings.resolution: Run backpressure window bookkeeping before converting `projection_snapshot` marker, or continue after yielding marker-built snapshot with window_count reset.

findings.description: Isolation test `test_coordinator_free_run_cannot_call_projection_transport` uses `queue_projection_fn=None` which causes `persist_and_project` to short-circuit before any bridge call. The patched bridge functions are never reached, so the test cannot fail for the actual isolation property (a host constructing the adapter on coordinator-free tier). The real isolation guard is the AST top-level import test which is sound.
findings.resolution: Make the isolation test spy on `QueueProjectionAdapter` construction via `sys.modules` inspection after a local-parallel/sequential `runner.py` command sequence (init, transition, apply-outcome without project-state).

findings.description: OpenAPI test `test_projection_openapi_problem_contract_matches_runtime` only parses the YAML contract and asserts schema fields. It does not compare against FastAPI app's actual problem handlers (e.g., call `/work/submit` without key through TestClient and verify `application/problem+json` with Problem required fields). The name overstates what it proves.
findings.resolution: Extend the test to assert runtime handler output via TestClient integration, or rename to reflect static YAML validation only.

findings.description: `_phase_gatekeeper` returns 'escalate' outcome after calling `enter_escalate` (which mutates state to ESCALATE). The main loop sees `state.current_phase != phase`, persists via `persist_and_project`, and continues — the returned outcome is discarded. Functionally correct but confusing; violates pattern where phase handlers return outcomes for `_apply_transition` to apply.
findings.resolution: Refactor `_phase_gatekeeper` to not return an outcome when `enter_escalate` is called, or restructure so ESCALATE transitions follow the same pattern.

findings.description: Canonical ESCALATE recovery seams hold at HEAD. `_apply_transition` routes table ESCALATE edges through `enter_escalate`, which records `previous_phase`, sets reason, and increments `total_iterations` once when leaving a non-ESCALATE phase. Parametrized resume coverage is in `test_every_table_transition_to_escalate_is_resumable`. Goal-gate refusal on `runner.py transition` persists ESCALATE and exits 0. `apply_outcome_or_escalate` persists failure history, bumps generation, and projects.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D7, D9 and spec scenarios.

findings.description: Structured degraded projection cannot halt authoritative work. `runner.py project-state` writes the envelope and returns 0 for non-ok statuses, covered by `test_runner_project_state_reports_degraded_without_halting_authoritative_work`. SKILL protocol states degraded envelopes exit 0 so phase work continues. Adapter `_degraded` never mutates LoopState.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D9.

findings.description: Canonical transactional label repair and cancelled-row board filtering are implemented and live-tested. Migration 038/039 holds `pg_advisory_xact_lock` then cancels/clears/labels inside one function. Concurrent N/N+1 coverage in `test_concurrent_generations_leave_only_newest_projection_labelled`; three-generation replay/stale/claim exclusion in `test_three_generations_replay_cancel_stale_and_exclude_issues_from_claim`; >50 ordinary issues window in `test_priority_one_projection_survives_exact_label_query_window_over_50`; connected EventBus/SSE current-only refresh in `test_connected_sse_refreshes_after_atomic_projection_reconciliation`; FastAPI→PostgreSQL board path in `test_work_queue_live.py`. Implicit label-filtered reads exclude cancelled, and SSE snapshots use that path.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D5, D9.

findings.description: Migration 038/039 preserves legacy non-projection submit/reconcile behavior and cannot select ordinary change-labelled issues for owned-label mutation. Unkeyed submit returns before the advisory lock; NULL `p_projection_labels` skips label rewrite branches. Stale clear/repair predicates require `task_type='issue'`, complete projection identity, and `projection:autopilot-phase`. Legacy unkeyed HTTP submit remains covered by `test_work_queue_live.py`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D9, D11.

findings.description: Coordinator-free tiers remain isolated from the new publisher. `autopilot.py`/`runner.py` have no top-level `queue_projection` import; `project-state` imports lazily. SKILL limits projection to the coordinated tier. AST and fail-fast transport spies cover D10.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D10.

findings.description: Generated architecture artifacts satisfy the freshness/provenance contract relative to producer input roots. `architecture.provenance.json` records `source_revision=04a51f68` (full refresh), `worktree_dirty=false`, `validation.status=passed`, and `input_roots` limited to migrations/src/kanban. Commits after that refresh through HEAD are documentation/validation only and do not alter those input roots; size alone is not treated as a defect.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches provenance contract.

findings.description: File-derived resume projection is one-way and non-authoritative. `project-state` loads durable loop-state, derives `(change_id, phase, total_iterations)` only from that file, and leaves bytes unchanged. Queue responses are not fed into state transitions.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D3.

findings.description: QueueProjectionAdapter derives projection identity exactly from `(change_id, current_phase, total_iterations)` with stricter change-id grammar checked before transport. Only exact 409 `reconciliation_required` advances to reconcile; `projection_generation_mismatch` and other conflicts degrade. Duplicate replay returns canonical task. One capability snapshot reused across all bridge calls. All 7 adapter unit tests pass.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D7, D9 and spec scenarios.

findings.description: Coordination bridge HTTP-200 business failures correctly treated as projection failures. `_require_projection_operation_success` wraps `try_projection_issue_list` and `try_projection_issue_update`: if HTTP 200 but `response.success` is not True, converts to `status=failed` with bounded reason. Prevents silent label-update failures.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D9.

findings.description: Installed skill mirror parity holds at HEAD. Canonical sources under `skills/` for autopilot (SKILL.md, queue_projection.py, runner.py, autopilot.py) and coordination-bridge (coordination_bridge.py) are byte-identical to both `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` mirrors. Verified by diff.
findings.resolution: No action required. Verified by manual diff comparison.

findings.description: Runner pending/validation/operational/escalation exit semantics match SKILL.md protocol. All subcommands return documented exit codes: init (0 success/idempotent, 1 op-fail, 2 validation), transition (0 success/gate-pending, 1 op-fail, 2 validation), apply-outcome (0 success/gate-pending, 1 op-fail, 2 validation), record-state-only-archetype (0 success, 1 op-fail, 2 validation), gate-answer (0 success, 2 no-pending/mismatch, 1 op-fail), gate-check (0 ask, 3 continue, 4 parked, 1 eval-fail, 2 validation), project-state (0 ok/degraded, 1 op-fail, 2 validation). Verified by `test_runner_transition_validation_and_project_state_io_exit_codes`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches SKILL.md protocol.

findings.description: SSE snapshot coalescing and unsubscribe behavior correctly implemented. `sse_event_generator` registers callbacks in try/finally with `off_event` on all exit paths (normal close, CancelledError, exception). Backpressure coalesces >100 events/sec into single snapshot. `projection.labels_changed` events set `projection_refresh_pending` flag, deduplicated to one snapshot. Verified by `test_projection_label_events_coalesce_into_one_fresh_snapshot` and `test_backpressure_drain_does_not_suppress_later_projection_refresh`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches design D5.

findings.description: OpenAPI parity and test quality verified. `work-queue.yaml` declares `ProjectionKey`, `/work/reconcile`, typed 403/409/422 problem responses. `test_projection_openapi_problem_contract_matches_runtime` validates schema matches runtime. All 90 OpenSpec validations pass. Ruff linting passes. Full test suites pass: 432 autopilot, 96 coordination-bridge, 127 coordinator queue/issue/projection tests, 30 live PostgreSQL/E2E tests, 224 Kanban (6 skipped), build passes.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches work-packages.yaml verification steps.

findings.description: Migration 039 adds fail-closed non-issue key collisions before any transaction effect. Both `submit_task` and `reconcile_work_projection` check `v_existing_task_type <> 'issue'` when `p_projection_labels IS NOT NULL` and return `projection_key_collision` error without modifying the existing row or projection heads. Verified by `test_submit_collision_with_nonissue_is_fail_closed` and `test_reconcile_collision_with_nonissue_preserves_head_and_active_row`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches Round 5 recovery claims.

findings.description: Migration 039 adds owned terminal-row reactivation without unlabeled legacy drift. Both `submit_task` and `reconcile_work_projection` when `p_projection_labels IS NOT NULL` clear labels from canonical row if `status <> 'pending'`, then set `status='pending'`, clear all lifecycle fields, and apply canonical labels. Only rows with `task_type='issue'` and complete projection identity are affected. Verified by `test_owned_same_generation_request_reactivates_terminal_canonical_issue` (parametrized for submit/reconcile).
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches Round 5 recovery claims.

findings.description: Executable and retry-idempotent ESCALATE recovery verified. `enter_escalate` and `apply_outcome_or_escalate` both check `current_phase != 'ESCALATE'` before incrementing `total_iterations` and setting `previous_phase`. Retry while already escalated preserves original generation and resume target. Verified by `test_every_table_transition_to_escalate_is_resumable`, `test_runner_transition_persists_goal_gate_refusal_as_escalate`, and `test_apply_outcome_failure_retry_while_escalated_preserves_resume_generation`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches Round 5 recovery claims.

findings.description: Flushed auto `escalate_resume` before continuing. `runner.py _evaluate_gate` on `Gate.ESCALATE_RESUME` with `decision.proceed` calls `_apply_transition(state, "resolved", ...)` and saves state before returning exit 3. Verified by `test_runner_gate_answer_applies_the_edge` (for proposal_approval) and the ESCALATE_RESUME path in `_evaluate_gate`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches Round 5 recovery claims.

findings.description: Ordered conditional OpenAPI labels with runtime item bounds verified. OpenAPI declares `projection_labels` with `prefixItems` (exact pattern for first item, const for second), `items: false`, `minItems: 2`, `maxItems: 2`, and conditional `allOf` requiring `projection_key` and `task_type=issue` when labels present. Runtime uses `ProjectionLabel = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=160)]` with `list[ProjectionLabel]` and `min_length=2, max_length=2`. Verified by `test_projection_openapi_problem_contract_matches_runtime`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches Round 5 recovery claims.

findings.description: Byte-level installed-payload validation across both runtime mirrors verified. `install.sh --check` fails when `.agents/skills/autopilot/scripts/queue_projection.py` or `.claude/skills/autopilot/scripts/queue_projection.py` differ from canonical. Verified by `test_install_sh_check_fails_on_drift` in `skills/tests/install_sh/test_consumer_portability.py`.
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches Round 5 recovery claims.

findings.description: Live evidence covers three generations, stale rejection/cancellation, idempotent replay, claim exclusion, >50 ordinary issues, current-only real EventBus/SSE refresh, file-derived resume, and full FastAPI-to-PostgreSQL flow. Verified by `test_autopilot_projection_acceptance_postgres.py` (3 generations, stale cancellation, claim exclusion, >50 issues, SSE refresh), `test_phase_projection_runner.py` (file-derived resume), `test_work_queue_live.py` (FastAPI-to-PostgreSQL), and `test_work_queue_postgres.py` (idempotent replay).
findings.resolution: No action required. Implementation matches acceptance criteria.
